hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-02 16:00 UTC | Duration 42m | Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Ruiz (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Cormorant CTO), Liam Ortega (ML Eng), Priya Singh (Head Infra)

00:00 - Samir: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, appreciate it. quick agenda, want to understand current token volumes, budget constraints and the hosting options that make most sense. elena will cover technical levers.
00:18 - Maya: thanks, yeah excited. we— um — we have pretty fragmented budgets. two product teams, one for insights chat and one for summarization. both bill into different buckets, so procurement is painful. target is roughly $20k per month for initial pilot across both.
00:34 - Liam: to add, our latency SLO for the chat path is 200 to 400 ms p95, and we need sub-second for the front end. throughput peaks about 40 rps during business hours.
00:51 - Elena: okay. that's helpful. on the hosting front, there are three general options — hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, or private vpc on-prem. each has cost/latency tradeoffs.
01:10 - Priya: security note — we need SOC2, SSO via SAML, KMS integration for key management, and audit logs forwarded to our splunk. also data residency for EU customers.
01:28 - Samir: we have SOC2 and can provide SOC2 report, SAML SSO, and KMS integrations. for residency we can run private control plane in region or a private deployment.
01:41 - Maya: the tricky part is the $20k cap. what's realistic for the hosted model per token? and what levers do we actually pull to reduce burn?
01:56 - Elena: per-token pricing depends on model and sequence length. ballpark hosted list for 7B-ish open models is X per 1k tokens (note: placeholder), but important levers are batching, prefix caching and using quantized variants. batching improves throughput and reduces per-token compute cost, but there's latency tradeoff if you wait too long to batch. prefix/K V cache — kv as in key value cache — reduces repeated attention for long dialogues by reusing cached KV state on the GPU. that can cut tokens billed to the model runtime if you do prefix caching at the platform layer.
02:28 - Liam: can you give an example? our chat has long histories sometimes 3–4k tokens.
02:36 - Elena: sure. suppose you have a 3k token prefix and 150 token user prompt. with no caching you re-compute the prefix each request and that's expensive. with prefix or kv caching the runtime stores the kv cache and you only compute for the new 150 tokens. that can be a 5–8x reduction in per-request token compute. transcription note: sometimes the platform billing still counts tokens for request + response but runtime cost is lowered.
03:05 - Maya: so that would dramatically change the unit economics. is that available on hosted?
03:11 - Samir: yes, prefix/K V cache is available on hosted and dedicated. dedicated gives you predictable throughput and slightly lower unit cost if you commit capacity. private gives you ultimate control but requires more ops and usually a platform fee.
03:24 - Priya: we prefer not to manage GPUs ourselves if we can avoid it but might consider private for residency. does dedicated let us pin model versions?
03:33 - Elena: yes, you can pin model versions and configure rollout policies. dedicated also supports configurable autoscaling and burst tiers.
03:41 - Liam: about quantization — any caveats? our summarization model is sensitive to quality.
03:47 - Elena: quantization to 4-bit or 8-bit is effective for many models but can introduce subtle regressions. our Optimize tooling can recommend profile per workload and we support A/B rollouts so you can measure quality delta on your eval set.
04:05 - Samir: back to cost: with your $20k pilot target we usually recommend starting hosted with committed discounts, and then move to dedicated if sustained volume or strict residency is required. Hosted gets you going with low ops overhead, dedicated buys you unit-cost predictability.
04:19 - Maya: committed discounts — what's the minimum commit? we have fragmented budgets so committing org-wide is hard.
04:27 - Samir: commits can be scoped to a team or product route. you can have separate commits per team which map to different cost centers. also there's a flexible burst to handle spikes.
04:36 - Priya: will that require cross-org signoff? I want to minimize procurement cycles.
04:42 - Samir: we can do a pilot MOU with lighter procurement and a timeboxed commit for the pilot. procurement typically requires a PO for a reserved capacity contract but for pilot we have a simpler contract.
04:55 - Liam: technical question — how does routing/fallback work if the dedicated pool is saturated?
05:02 - Elena: we do smart routing by policy. a request can fail-over to a compatible hosted instance or to a lower-cost/latency model variant. fallback preserves availability but may change latency or cost characteristics. you can set route policies to prefer latency or cost.
05:16 - Maya: how about per-token billing vs per-inference? i need to explain to finance.
05:22 - Samir: hosted is per-token plus any per-request overhead for streaming. Dedicated is usually a reserved capacity fee that you amortize across tokens — effectively per-token cost = (reserved cost + variable infra)/tokens. We'll model both for your volumes.
05:35 - Priya: can we get a worked example? like if we commit $10k to dedicated and run 200M tokens per month what's our unit?
05:42 - Elena: we'll run that calculation offline — it depends on model family and batch efficiency. the key is batching: if your average user session is micro-interactions under 30 tokens, batching yields limited wins; but for longer generation or when we can queue micro-batches we see 2–3x improvements. also KV cache multiplies benefits for long history chats.
06:05 - Maya: okay. one of the constraints is that each product team has separate card payments and they're very conservative. is there a way to map spend by route so each team gets billed separately?
06:16 - Samir: yes, route-level metering and token-level cost breakdown in Console lets you attribute spend per API key or per route. we also integrate with billing exports and can push to your billing system.
06:29 - Liam: about benchmarks — what telemetry do you need?
06:33 - Elena: for a bench run we'll need representative prompt sets, typical sequence length distribution, p95 latency SLO, and a traffic shape (rps spikes). we'll then run hosted and a dedicated proof-of-cost with prefix cache enabled to show delta.
06:50 - Samir: any blockers from your side for doing that bench?
06:53 - Maya: we need to clear procurement for the pilot spend but for the bench we can use a dev card. main blocker is consolidating token volumes by team.
07:02 - Samir: action: Maya to share volumes by 11/06, we'll turn around a tailored pricing and bench plan.
07:10 - Priya: one more infra detail — we need VPC peering or private link to avoid public egress for EU traffic. do you support that in hosted?
07:19 - Elena: hosted supports private link for enterprise plans; dedicated supports VPC peering and private deployments can be fully air-gapped. there's some networking setup lead time for peering.
07:32 - Liam: what about key management? can we bring our KMS or do you host keys?
07:36 - Samir: both. for hosted we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations; for private/on-prem you control HSM/KMS.
07:45 - Maya: great. are there any hidden costs — like per-route logging or observability add-ons?
07:51 - Elena: we have add-ons: extended retention for observability, advanced evals, and premium SLA. those can be optional for the pilot. we will call them out in the pricing.
08:03 - Samir: i'll put together a concise pricing deck that shows hosted with commit, dedicated reserved example, and private ballpark. we'll include a modeled unit cost table for your 3 volume scenarios.
08:13 - Maya: sounds good. what's a realistic timeline to show us numbers and run the bench?
08:18 - Samir: we'll aim to send pricing and SOC2 + security docs by 11/04, schedule technical deep dive and bench for week of 11/09, bench results by 11/12. does that work?
08:28 - Maya: yes, that's fine.
08:31 - Priya: please include our compliance contact in the docs.
08:34 - Samir: will do.
08:36 - Elena: quick note on model quantization — for your summarization flows, we'll propose running a small A/B on 4-bit quantized vs fp16 to see if quality holds. Optimize can flag regressions.
08:49 - Liam: okay. any competitor concerns? we've looked at Anthropic's managed offering and Vertex for tight GCP integration.
08:57 - Samir: noted. we'll include a differentiation slide focusing on predictable unit economics and observability per-route which helps with fragmented budgets.
09:07 - Maya: last question — can we do separate commits per team but single invoice? procurement prefers single invoice.
09:14 - Samir: yes, we can centralize invoicing while mapping commits to internal cost centers.
09:20 - Maya: okay that helps. thanks, everyone.
09:25 - Samir: recap: Samir send pricing + SOC2 + network diagram by 11/04; Elena schedule bench and prepare telemetry template; Maya share token volumes and SLOs by 11/06. meeting adjourned.

End of transcript. Notes: there are a few transcription artifacts: "kv" spelled as "K V" sometimes, quantization occasionally transcribed as "quantizashun", and product names generalized.
